subject: Rebaseline: POC scope and success criteria for Acme Analytics trial
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Collins <sam.collins@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Priya Ramesh <priya.ramesh@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: POC follow-up + proposed success criteria (Acme)

Hi Sam / Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to hear more about the analytics pipeline and the two primary goals you want to validate in the POC: (1) batch embedding similarity for historical search, and (2) streaming embeddings for near-real-time alerts.

Recap / proposed POC scope (2 weeks):
- Use case A: Batch reindex of 6 months of data (~25M tokens) into Redwood embeddings; compare recall/precision against existing system. Success criteria: >= 10% lift in mean reciprocal rank (MRR) on your top-20 queries, and inference cost at or below $0.002 per request.
- Use case B: Streaming alerts for critical events (latency-sensitive). Success criteria: 95th percentile end-to-end latency < 400ms for a 128-token prompt under target throughput (20qps).

Owners: Redwood: Marissa (PM)/Dev Patel (solutions) — Acme: Sam (product), Priya (SRE).
Next steps:
1) I attached a short success_criteria spreadsheet with measurement details (see poc_success_criteria_v2.xlsx).
2) Dev will confirm infra and quantization profile needed by Fri.
3) Kickoff POC on Monday 25 May if all good.

If anything above looks off or you'd like to add a quick use case to the scope, flag it here.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: poc_success_criteria_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Sam Collins <sam.collins@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Ramesh <priya.ramesh@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC follow-up + proposed success criteria (Acme)

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Couple of quick asks after syncing with the product team:

1) Can we add a third, smaller use case mid-trial: "reranking for nearline recommendations"? This would be lower volume but the success criteria are business-facing (CTR lift on the top 5 recommendations). We can provide a held-out dataset.
2) For the streaming latency, can you confirm whether the 400ms target includes network time to our VPC or is purely inference? We need it end-to-end if possible.

If adding the reranking use case will require more time, we can prioritize the batch and streaming first and scope reranking as a follow-up; happy to be flexible but wanted to flag it now.

—Sam
Sam Collins
Product Manager, Acme Analytics

- For latency, what we can measure by default vs. what requires a VPC/proxy measurement?

Marissa

"(see above)"

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Collins <sam.collins@acmeanalytics.com>, Priya Ramesh <priya.ramesh@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: POC follow-up + proposed success criteria (Acme)

Marissa / team — quick feasibility note after running this past infra:

1) Reranking (low volume): technically feasible to include as an additional evaluation if we limit to a held-out offline dataset (no streaming). We'll need an extra day to wire the reranking eval and add it to the success_criteria sheet. It should not impact infrastructure costs materially.

2) End-to-end latency: By default our hosted telemetry measures inference-only latency. To get true E2E (including network + client-side) we need either: (a) a lightweight agent in Acme's VPC to emit synthetic requests, or (b) run the streaming test over your VPN endpoint with Priya's team capturing ingress timing. Option (a) requires a quick firewall rule and an agent (we can provide a one-file python script) — estimate 1 business day to validate.

3) Timeline impact: with reranking added and the agent for E2E, I recommend rebaselining the POC to 3 weeks to ensure proper measurement and regression testing. Proposed new milestones:
- Week 1: Batch reindex + baseline metrics
- Week 2: Streaming integration + agent for E2E latency
- Week 3: Reranking eval + final analysis and handoff

I've attached a short implementation note with infra steps and an updated measurement plan (technical_implementation_notes.pdf).

If that timeline is acceptable I'll update the success_criteria spreadsheet and propose new kickoff and demo dates.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: technical_implementation_notes.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Collins <sam.collins@acmeanalytics.com>, Priya Ramesh <priya.ramesh@acmeanalytics.com>

Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Rebaseline approved: updated POC plan + owners (Acme)

Hi Sam / Priya — following internal review, we can accommodate the reranking use case and end-to-end latency measurement, but we'll need to extend the POC to 3 weeks to keep the measurement signal clean. Updated plan below: 

Updated POC (3 weeks):
- Week 1 (batch): Reindex 6 months of data, measure MRR on top-20 queries. Owner: Marissa / Acme data team.
- Week 2 (streaming): Integrate streaming path; run E2E tests via the provided agent. Owner: Dev / Priya.
- Week 3 (reranking): Offline reranking evaluation on held-out set; measure CTR proxy lift and operational cost. Owner: Neha / Acme product.

Updated success criteria are in the attached spreadsheet (poc_success_criteria_v2.xlsx) — I added a reranking tab and clarified that latency targets are end-to-end when run through the agent.

Next steps / action items:
- Priya: confirm firewall rules for the agent and share an accessible test endpoint by Wed 27 May.
- Dev: share agent script and infra checklist (ETA Tue 26 May).
- Sam: confirm dataset for reranking (shared Drive link is fine).

Proposed kickoff: Monday 1 June. Proposed demo: Friday 19 June.

If that looks good I'll update the HubSpot deal and calendar invites.

Best,
Marissa
